components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Expand and collapse supporting information without losing keyboard access.
components.purpose: Put long secondary content behind a short, named control so a page stays scannable while the content remains reachable.
whenToUse: Secondary guidance is long enough to interrupt the primary task.
The heading of each disclosure makes sense without the hidden content.
People need to compare several short sections without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: The content is essential to every user on first read; keep it visible.
You need to hide a single sentence; plain text is less work.
The control would be used as a menu, filter, or navigation pattern.
implementation: Use a real button inside a heading; never a div with a click handler.
Give the button aria-controls pointing at a unique panel id.
Keep aria-expanded in sync with the panel's visible state.
Use the official USWDS accordion JavaScript rather than a lookalike handler.
keyboard: Tab reaches each disclosure button once.
Enter and Space both toggle the panel.
Focus stays on the button after toggling.
No keyboard trap is created inside the panel.
preferences: The panel stays readable when text is resized and when JavaScript is unavailable.
Reduced motion must not remove essential state feedback.
Forced colors must keep the boundary and focus indicator visible.
mistakes: Styling a link as a disclosure or omitting the button element.
Updating visual state without updating aria-expanded.
Duplicating ids when the same component appears twice.
Treating the loading-state flash as solved when scripts fail.
testing: Test every collapsed and expanded state with a real key press.
Test content availability with JavaScript disabled.
Test with 200% text, forced colors, and a narrow viewport.
limitations: This fixture is author-created markup using official USWDS assets, not a byte-for-byte copy of an upstream example.
The baseline is rendered with a small fixture stylesheet for consistent page framing.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: Communicate status, warnings and errors with meaning beyond color.
components.purpose: Draw attention to a short message that relates to the current task or page without blocking the rest of the interface.
whenToUse: A short message must stay visible near the task it affects.
A warning or error needs an explicit heading and next step.
whenNotToUse: The message is a transient success confirmation; use a status message.
The content is long-form guidance; use prose or a callout.
The alert would interrupt a flow that already has an error summary.
implementation: Choose the alert variant by meaning, not decoration.
Include a heading that makes sense without the icon or border color.
Do not add a live region to a static alert; use role=status or role=alert only for the state change that warrants it.
keyboard: Static alerts add no tab stops.
If an alert contains a link or button, that control follows normal keyboard order.
A live alert must not steal focus.
preferences: Meaning must survive without color, including forced colors.
Text must remain readable at 200% and in dark themes.
mistakes: Relying on the colored left border to distinguish warning from error.
Putting an entire error summary inside every inline alert.
Using role=alert for content that is present on page load.
testing: Read each variant without seeing color and confirm the heading carries the meaning.
Measure text and boundary contrast in every supported theme.
limitations: Dynamic and updated alerts are local demonstrations; announcement behaviour has not been verified with a real screen reader.
The experimental theme does not yet recolour the upstream alert icon.
The Arabic state is one direction and language sample; native-language review is outstanding.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: Distinguish a government-service identity pattern from ordinary site content.
components.purpose: Give a service a consistent identity area at the top of the page, including a short explanation of the site's official status.
whenToUse: A site needs the standard USWDS identity pattern.
The banner can make an accurate statement about the service.
whenNotToUse: The banner would imply government endorsement that does not exist.
A marketing header is needed instead.
implementation: Keep the official banner structure and disclosure button.
Use the correct language and direction for the page.
Do not recolor agency logos or identity marks without authorization.
keyboard: The disclosure button is reachable once and toggles with Enter or Space.
The banner content remains readable without JavaScript.
preferences: Test logical direction, not just mirrored layout.
Keep text and controls legible in dark and forced-colors modes.
mistakes: Using the banner for a private product with a false official claim.
Reversing the entire page visually instead of using logical properties.
Hard-coding English text in a shared banner include.
testing: Test the disclosure in LTR and RTL.
Check narrow layouts at 320 CSS pixels.
limitations: The demo copy is deliberately neutral and is not a government identity.
The RTL prototype uses sample Arabic content; a native-language review is outstanding.

components.name: Form controls
components.summary: Labels, required controls, validation and legible focus states.
components.purpose: Collect a small amount of information with explicit labels, native validation, and a local-only submission path.
whenToUse: A short form needs visible labels and native constraint validation.
A demonstration must not send data to a live service.
whenNotToUse: The flow needs multi-step error recovery; add an error summary.
The field set is long enough to require a review step.
implementation: Associate every control with a visible label.
Use fieldset and legend for grouped radios or checkboxes.
Use native required and reportValidity rather than a custom validation widget.
Keep submission local in this lab; never post test data to a government endpoint.
keyboard: Tab reaches each control in reading order.
Arrow keys move within a native radio group.
Invalid submission leaves focus on a useful control.
preferences: Focus indicators must remain visible in every theme.
Text size and zoom must not clip labels or error text.
mistakes: Using placeholder text as the only label.
Hiding the radio input in a way that removes focus or Voice Control access.
Marking required fields with an unexplained asterisk.
testing: Submit empty, correct one field, submit valid.
Test keyboard-only completion and focus after validation.
Test the browser's native validation message in at least two engines.
limitations: Native validation messaging differs by browser and is not controlled by this lab.
Voice Control testing has not been performed by a person.

components.name: Radio validation
components.summary: Investigate required radio groups, native constraint validation, and focus placement.
components.purpose: Reproduce how a required radio group behaves when a form is submitted with no selection, including where focus lands and what the browser exposes.
whenToUse: A required choice must be made before submission.
The team wants to rely on native browser validation rather than a custom widget.
whenNotToUse: The group is optional; do not mark it required to demonstrate validation.
A custom validation pattern is already in place and tested.
implementation: Use a fieldset and legend for the group.
Put required on the native radio inputs.
Do not add redundant aria-required to native required inputs.
Let the browser prevent submission and report the invalid control.
keyboard: Arrow keys move between radio options.
Submitting an empty group leaves focus on the first invalid radio in tested browsers.
preferences: The visible radio boundary and focus ring must meet non-text contrast.
Native validation bubbles are browser-controlled and may not be customizable.
mistakes: Adding role=radiogroup or aria-required to a native fieldset without evidence.
Assuming every browser moves focus to the same element.
testing: Submit with no selection and record document.activeElement.
Select with the keyboard and submit successfully.
Test in Chromium and Firefox; record the browser-specific result.
limitations: Voice Control and real screen-reader confirmation remain outstanding.
The lab records browser behavior; it does not change upstream radio positioning.

experiments.title: Native dark-mode support
experiments.summary: A semantic token layer that lets USWDS components respond to system appearance and an explicit user override without replacing upstream components.

review.decision: Accepted as a lab experiment; upstream not authorized.

concerns: Header, footer, navigation, cards, tables, and the upstream alert icon are not themed yet.

experiments.title: User preferences panel
experiments.summary: A proposed component that gives people a consistent way to choose appearance, text size, contrast, and motion without a third-party overlay.

concerns: Stored-preference failure handling and cross-tab behaviour remain unreviewed.

experiments.title: Logical properties for RTL support
experiments.summary: Replace selected physical left/right styles in the banner and alert with logical properties so right-to-left layouts do not depend on mirrored overrides.

concerns: Native-language review of the RTL sample is outstanding.

experiments.title: Native radio validation
experiments.summary: A focused reproduction of required radio-group submission, native constraint validation, and browser focus placement.

concerns: Voice Control and real screen-reader testing are outstanding.

scenarios.intent: Use keyboard to open disclosure and confirm its state is exposed
Read alert without relying on color alone
Submit required fields and inspect native feedback
